findings.subject: ai-planning/design-briefs/2026-09-10-review-readiness-simplified-contract.md
findings.impact: The latest committed brief declares the planning-artifact rebuild done, but its commit tree contains none of the active change directory; the only copy is untracked. A durable record therefore asserts completion that a later reviewer cannot reproduce from the cited revision.
findings.recommendation: Do not mark the rebuild done until the exact artifact set has a durable binding. Either commit the planning directory before the claim or record it as explicitly pending with a reproducible artifact manifest and make the later entry gate verify that binding.

findings.subject: docs/design/glossary/05-validation-and-recovery.md
findings.impact: The working tree already adds the two glossary entries assigned to Apply task 4.1, although the proposal says this change creates planning artifacts only and task 4.1 depends on task 1.1, which itself depends on the gated task 0.1. This crosses the Planning-to-Apply boundary in the primary worktree and makes the current packet inconsistent with its own task graph.
findings.recommendation: Remove or isolate the task-4.1 implementation edits from the pre-Apply workspace. Reintroduce them only through the registered delivery worktree after the required approval and preservation-delivery gate are evidenced.

findings.subject: openspec/changes/establish-streamlined-review-readiness/design.md
findings.impact: The design calls the task-5.2 review record a change-owned working file and not a delivered path, while task 5.2 requires committing it so it is delivered and task 6.1 makes it part of the pull-request scope set. The same file consequently has incompatible delivery semantics, leaving the claimed authoritative scope check ambiguous.
findings.recommendation: Choose one model and use it consistently: classify the review record as a delivered provenance artifact outside the guidance inventory, or keep it out of the delivery branch and exclude it from the pull-request set. Update the design, task evidence, and scope-observation record together.

findings.subject: openspec/changes/establish-streamlined-review-readiness/tasks.md
findings.impact: Task 0.1 says its prerequisite delivery contains every preserved record cited by the plan but verifies only 713553d. The scope-observation design review and the governing-record reconciliation were added later in df8c0b7 and a42215f; a base can satisfy the pinned check while lacking the current governing decision or its revised sources.
findings.recommendation: Bind the entry gate to the exact preservation revision that contains the final cited sources, or to a versioned manifest of those sources and their digests. Do not accept path existence alone as proof that the current governing content was delivered.
